name: metR
description: Tools for Easier Analysis of Meteorological Fields

paragraphs: metR packages several functions and utilities that make R better for handling meteorological data in the tidy data paradigm. It started mostly sa a packaging of assorted wrappers and tricks that I wrote for my day to day work as a researcher in atmospheric sciences. Since then, it has grown organically and for my own needs and feedback from users.

Conceptually it’s divided into visualization tools and data tools. The former are geoms, stats and scales that help with plotting using ggplot2, such as statcontourfill() or scaleylevel(), while the later are functions for common data processing tools in the atmospheric sciences, such as Derivate() or EOF(); these are implemented to work in the data.table paradigm, but also work with regular data frames.

Currently metR is in development but maturing. Most functions check arguments and there are some tests. However, some functions might change it’s interface, and functionality can be moved to other packages, so please bear that in mind.
